For it is not right that the conferral of the sacred order should become for Christ’s servants a cause of arrogance and earthly pleasure, since they find nothing of this kind either in the words or in the examples of the Master himself or of his disciples.

Let us hear how the apostle Paul instructs us concerning Christ’s character [Col. 1203D]:

> “Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus. Although he was in the form of God, he did not consider equality with God something to be seized, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of human beings and found in appearance as a human being. He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death—even death on a cross. Therefore God also exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father” (Philippians 2; the supplied text reads “Philip. X”).

Therefore he commanded his disciples, saying:

> “Do not be anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’ For the Gentiles seek all these things. Your Father knows that you need all these things. Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added [Col. 1204A] to you” (Matthew 6).

> “Whoever does not renounce everything that he possesses cannot be my disciple” (Luke 14).

> “Whoever wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it. For what does it profit a person if he gains the whole world but suffers the loss of his soul? etc.” (Luke 19).

For this reason Peter also exhorts the faithful in his Epistle, saying:

> “Girding the loins of your mind, being perfectly sober, hope in the grace offered to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ, as obedient children, not conforming yourselves to the former desires of your ignorance, but according to the one who called you, the Holy One, be holy yourselves in all your conduct, because it is written: ‘You shall be holy, for I am holy’” (1 Peter 1).

John likewise says [Col. 1204B]:

> “Do not love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him, because everything that is in the world—the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away, and its desire; but whoever does the will of God remains forever” (1 John 2).

Paul also says:

> “Therefore let sin not reign in your mortal body, so as to obey its desires. Do not present your members to sin as weapons of iniquity, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members as weapons of righteousness [Col. 1204C] to God” (Romans 5–6).

And again:

> “Make no provision for the flesh in its desires” (Romans 13).

And again:

> “Let us no longer judge one another, but judge this rather: that you should not place a stumbling block or scandal before your brother” (Romans 14).

And again:

> “We who are stronger ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak and not to please ourselves. Let each of us please his neighbor for his good, for edification” (Romans 15).

If, then, in accordance with this teaching, [Col. 1204D] we conform ourselves to the examples of Christ’s obedience, humility, and gentleness, each of us considering not what is useful to us but what is useful to others, and devoting ourselves neither to the desires nor to the enticements of this world, there will be no contention among us over superiority of honor, empty boasting of earthly power, or wicked conflict over the profit of the present age.

Instead, firm peace and concord will exist among us; the worship of piety will be practiced unanimously; and holy, undefiled religion before God—while we await heavenly glory at the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ and Savior—will be preserved without reproach.

Thus all the members of Christ’s body will be at peace. Though we do not see him, we love him; though we do not now see him, we believe in him and rejoice in hope, trusting that at his coming we shall receive the end of our faith, the salvation of our souls.

Therefore, since the order of your preceding account [Col. 1205A] and of our humble reply required us to excerpt something from the sacred Scriptures and from the judgments of orthodox Fathers against so senseless a conflict among priests and so great a scandal among the people—passages that would show and make clear that Christ’s servants ought not to quarrel, but should be gentle toward all, teachable, and patient—we have done what we judged ought to be done.

We have gathered these matters into a short booklet [Col. 1206A] and have taken care to send it to your holiness, asking that, if you deem it worthy of reading, you confirm by your authority whatever has been correctly set down there; and if anything there appears worthy of correction, that your wisdom instruct the ignorant, so that in every respect our labor may not be in vain, and that our zeal for your teaching may be rewarded with manifold recompense by the giver of every good thing.

# Penitential

The Penitential begins. 471

**Chapter I.** On homicides committed deliberately. 471

**[Column 1209] Chapter V.** On administrators and those who dictate criminal petitions. 473  
**Chapter VI.** On the necessary offense committed by the people. 473  
**Chapter VII.** On parricide. 473

**Chapter IX.** On those who cause abortions. 474  
**Chapter X.** On those who commit capital crimes after receiving sacred orders, and on their penance or excommunication. 474  
**Chapter XI.** On priests who have taken wives or committed fornication. 480  
**Chapter XII.** On those who, violating their penance, again transgress. 481  
**Chapter XIII.** That forgiveness should be granted to penitents at the Lord’s Supper. 482

**Chapter XVIII.** On perjury. 484

**Chapter XXVI.** On those who have joined themselves to pagans or Jews. 490

**Chapter XXVIII.** On those who have both a wife and a concubine. 490
